CHIEF COMPLAINT
Back pain with right foot paresthesias.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient reports he was raking leaves in his yard yesterday and felt fine. Approximately two hours after coming inside, he developed back tightening and pins and needles sensation in his right foot. He had similar back pain approximately three years ago that resolved after one day. He has tried ice and two Advils without relief. Heat from a hot shower provided some relief. Pain improves when sitting. Pain present with forward bending but not with standing up. Tenderness to palpation around L5. Denies prolonged physical activity recently. Partner reports pain is worse when patient stands up. Patient notes high pain tolerance and would not complain unless significant.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Tingling sensation in right leg. No other systems reviewed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Back pain three years ago.

MEDICATIONS
Advil (over-the-counter, used for current pain without relief).

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient reports he normally does not do any physical activity. Engaged in yard work (raking leaves) yesterday, which is unusual for him.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Low back: Pain with forward flexion. No pain with extension. Tenderness to palpation at L5. Dorsiflexion normal. Pulses equal in all extremities.

RESULTS
X-ray of low back: Normal.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Low back strain. Plan: Rest. Prescribe meloxicam. Prescribe physical therapy to include stretches and exercises to improve fitness. Patient to contact physician if not improving. Follow-up in two weeks with consideration for MRI if symptoms persist.
